On physical exam, the right upper extremity blood pressure is 150/80 mm Hg. That seems high because, for a child, normal blood pressure can vary, but generally, a BP of 150/80 might be elevated. He has 2+ radial pulses and trace femoral pulses. Radial pulses are in the arms, and femoral are in the groin. 2+ might be normal, but trace could indicate something is a bit off. Maybe decreased femoral pulses could suggest something like coarctation of the aorta, which can cause reduced pulse strength in the lower extremities. A systolic murmur is heard between S1 and S2, and a ejection click is a click that occurs just after S1, often associated with aortic stenosis or sclerosis, or maybe a bicuspid aortic valve.
